raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: One-way ANOVA on perceived household indoor water use: peri-urban mean 263 lpcd vs. rural mean 206 lpcd (27% higher, p < 0.05, N = 965 households across 8 WSSs; PDF p. 10 & Fig. 6 p. 12); regression of perceived water use on SEC factors (household size, education, age, occupation) and binary peri-urban/rural zone: R^2 = 10% (household size, education, and zone significant, exact coefficients in unprinted Appendix 2; PDF p. 13).
raw_response.publication_year_note: Published 14 November 2024 in Frontiers in Water, Volume 6, Article 1389648 (received 21 February 2024; accepted 30 September 2024; copyright 2024).
raw_response.rationale: Full text (17 pages) is accessible and reports inferential statistics (one-way ANOVA with post-hoc comparisons, pairwise correlations with Holm adjustment, and a multiple regression summarized from Appendix 2 on N = 965 households across 8 community water supply systems in Cali and Restrepo, Colombia). However, none of the inferential tests evaluates a narrow Criterion 2 legal, tenure, tariff, administrative, regulatory, or ownership exposure. All 8 studied systems are formal community Water Users' Associations (WUAs), and the inferential analyses test only socio-economic/demographic household characteristics (household size, education, age, occupation) and spatial location/system IDs (peri-urban vs. rural zone defined by distance from Cali) against self-reported perceived indoor water use habits (estimated from self-reported fixture use durations and literature flow rates, assuming shower use even during intermittent supply). Institutional/regulatory attributes such as Water Use Efficiency Program (WUEP) adoption, WUA staffing, and billing are reported only descriptively across the 8 systems in Tables 2-3 without inferential testing. Thus, the study falls under inferential_non_swim_or_out_of_scope.
